newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LEONARD CLAIMS CREDIT FOR SUBDUING PUMAS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LEONARD CLAIMS CREDIT FOR SUBDUING PUMAS.

text.p: New captain Jason Leonard claimed personal credit for rescuing England from the brink of an embarrassing home defeat by Argentina at Twickenham on Saturday.

The home side were trailing 18-15 with less than eight minutes remaining when the England forwards finally punched a hole in the Pumas defence and drove over the line with Leonard and hooker Mark Regan at the bottom of the pile.

Regan was originally credited with his first international try but Leonard, who had also never scored in 51 matches for England, emerged afterwards to insist he was the man who had dragged his team from the Pumas' clutches.

"My first try for England in my first test as captain...now I'm going to go home and check my lottery numbers," said Leonard, happy to divert some attention away from another uninispiring England display in their final test of 1996.

In the corresponding fixture six years ago, England won 51- 0, but Leonard, deputising for the injured Phil de Glanville, admitted the Pumas could easily have scored the year's biggest international upset.
"They were a totally different kettle of fish today," Leonard said. "Last time they basically lay down and were terrified of the Twickenham crowd, but this team had no such problems."

Coach Jack Rowell's next game is not until February when Scotland visit Twickenham in the Five Nations championship, but he hinted at new faces after another demonstration of England's failure to obtain lift-off in the professional era.
Almost all the wit and invention came from the Pumas backs, and Argentine captain Lisandro Arbizu was not slow to point out the difference.
"We made some mistakes but we were much better than them. We should have scored a couple of tries," he said.
Young Pumas fly-half Gonzalo Quesada still took his side to the verge of a first win at Twickenham with six sweet penalties, and English discipline was frayed by the end.

They had a try from Jeremy Guscott disallowed following a punch from lock Martin Johnson and the same player was lucky to stay on the field after a swinging high tackle on Gonzalo Camardon near the end.
If Mike Catt, who otherwise had an undistinguished game, had not keep pace with Queseda's strike-rate, England would have struggled to shake off their tenacious opponents.

They even resorted to a desperate tactical substitution, bringing on Ben Clarke to beef up the back-row, but the Argentine pack gave nothing away and the whole Pumas side offered plenty of hope for the future.

England - 15-Nick Beal; 14-Jon Sleightholme, 13-Will Carling, 12-Jeremy Guscott, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt, 9- Andy Gomarsall; 8-Chris Sheasby (19-Ben Clarke, 56), 7-Lawrence Dallaglio, 6-Tim Rodber, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Martin Johnson, 3-Jason Leonard (captain), 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.

Argentina - 15-Ezequiel Jurado; 14-Gonzalo Camardon, 13- Eduardo Simone, 12-Lisandro Arbizu (captain), 11-Diego Albanese; 10-Gonzalo Queseda, 9-Nicolas Fernandez Miranda; 8-Pablo Bouza, 7-Pablo Camerlinckx, 6-Rolando Martin, 5-German Llanes, 4-Pedro Sporleder, 3-Mauricio Reggiardo, 2-Carlos Promanzio, 1-Roberto Grau.
